title: 2nd Matter The Criterion Of Scientific Consensus

questions.question: Who can speak with real authority in a science or art?
questions.answer: The people who truly know that field.

questions.question: Can a person outside that field give the final word about it?
questions.answer: No. That person is not the right expert for it.

questions.question: In the example, whose words about sickness matter more: an engineer’s or a doctor’s?
questions.answer: A doctor’s.

questions.question: Why is a philosopher focused only on physical things not a strong guide in spiritual matters?
questions.answer: Because he does not understand spiritual things well.

questions.question: What kind of matters are being talked about in this passage besides physical things?
questions.answer: Sacred and spiritual matters.

questions.question: Who are the “People of Truth” in this passage?
questions.answer: Many truthful spiritual people who know the matters of faith.

questions.question: What does the passage say these truthful people agree about?
questions.answer: They agree on sacred matters and Allah’s oneness.

questions.question: What is said about Shaykh Gilani’s spiritual life?
questions.answer: He worked for many years and reached high spiritual understanding.

questions.question: If many strong spiritual knowers agree, what does that do to weak objections from material-minded people?
questions.answer: It makes those objections seem very small.

questions.question: What picture is used to show how tiny those objections are?
questions.answer: A little insect sound compared with loud thunder.

questions.question: What is one main lesson of the whole passage?
questions.answer: The right experts should be trusted in spiritual matters.

questions.question: Why should a believer not feel shaken by such denials?
questions.answer: Because they come from people who are not qualified in that area.

questions.question: What is this passage mostly teaching about?
questions.answer: Who should be trusted when speaking about spiritual truth.

questions.question: Why can a learned person still be wrong outside his own field?
questions.answer: Because being smart in one area does not make him an expert in every area.

questions.question: What simple example helps explain this idea?
questions.answer: A builder or engineer is not the best person to cure illness.

questions.question: Who would even know more about disease than that engineer in this example?
questions.answer: Even a very low-ranking doctor.

questions.question: What kind of philosopher is criticized here?
questions.answer: One who only pays attention to material things.

questions.question: What happens to such a person’s understanding of spiritual things?
questions.answer: It becomes weak and far away from the truth.

questions.question: Why are his denials given little worth?
questions.answer: Because he is speaking about matters he cannot really see or grasp.

questions.question: What big truth do many holy and truthful people agree on?
questions.answer: They agree about faith and Allah’s unity.

questions.question: What does the passage say Shaykh Gilani reached through long spiritual effort?
questions.answer: Deep certainty in the truths of belief.

questions.question: What does the passage suggest about philosophers lost in tiny worldly details?
questions.answer: They become confused and cannot judge higher truths well.

questions.question: Which is stronger in the passage: the agreement of many spiritual knowers or the denial of philosophers?
questions.answer: The agreement of the spiritual knowers.

questions.question: What feeling should this give a Muslim child reading the passage?
questions.answer: Confidence in the truth of faith.

questions.question: If people are not trained in a subject, what does the passage say about their judgment?
questions.answer: It should not be taken as final.

questions.question: Does being great or famous make a person an expert in every topic?
questions.answer: No, it does not.

questions.question: What makes some philosophers poor judges of spiritual truths?
questions.answer: They stay busy only with things they can touch and see.

questions.question: According to the passage, what do they become less able to notice?
questions.answer: Non-material and spiritual realities.

questions.question: Who are said to be in complete agreement on holy matters?
questions.answer: Very many people of truth.

questions.question: What is special about Shaykh Gilani in this passage?
questions.answer: He had very high spiritual insight and long years of worshipful striving.

questions.question: How long is he said to have spent advancing in spiritual work?
questions.answer: Ninety years.

questions.question: After hearing about such people, how should we view the objections of material-focused philosophers?
questions.answer: As weak and not important.

questions.question: What sound comparison shows this weakness?
questions.answer: Their objections are like a tiny buzz next to thunder.

questions.question: What is the best short summary of the passage?
questions.answer: Trust true spiritual experts about spiritual truth.

questions.question: What kind of people cannot join the learned agreement of a field?
questions.answer: People who are outside that field.

questions.question: Why not?
questions.answer: Because they do not have the right knowledge for it.

questions.question: What does the passage compare to show this clearly?
questions.answer: It compares an engineer with a doctor.

questions.question: For finding and treating a sickness, whose judgment counts more?
questions.answer: The doctor’s judgment.

questions.question: What mistake do some philosophers make in this passage?
questions.answer: They try to speak strongly about spiritual things while only knowing material things.

questions.question: What are the other kinds of matters in the passage?
questions.answer: Holy and spiritual matters.

questions.question: What is said about the people of truth on these holy matters?
questions.answer: They are united and agree together.

questions.question: Why is Shaykh Gilani mentioned?
questions.answer: To show an example of a great spiritual knower.

questions.question: What does his long spiritual journey show?
questions.answer: That he had deep experience in faith.

questions.question: If expert spiritual people agree, what happens to the denials of people stuck in worldly details?
questions.answer: Those denials lose importance.

questions.question: What lesson should students learn from this?
questions.answer: Listen to the right experts in the right subjects.

questions.question: When people talk about science or art, who should be listened to most?
questions.answer: The people who truly know that subject.

questions.question: Can someone be wise and accomplished but still not be the right person to judge another field?
questions.answer: Yes. A person can be skilled in one area and not another.

questions.question: What example from the passage teaches this?
questions.answer: An engineer is not the best judge of a disease.

questions.question: Who is a better guide for sickness, even if he seems less important?
questions.answer: A doctor.

questions.question: What kind of person is not worth following in spiritual matters, according to the passage?
questions.answer: A philosopher who only thinks about the physical world.

questions.question: Why are his words weak in that area?
questions.answer: Because his mind is limited to what he can see with his eyes.

questions.question: What do the People of Truth agree on?
questions.answer: Sacred truths and Allah’s oneness.

questions.question: What does the passage say Shaykh Gilani was able to do spiritually?
questions.answer: He reached very high spiritual understanding.

questions.question: How does the passage describe philosophers lost in tiny worldly details?
questions.answer: As overwhelmed and confused.

questions.question: What two sounds are compared at the end of the passage?
questions.answer: A mosquito’s buzz and thunder.

questions.question: Why is that comparison used?
questions.answer: To show how small weak denials are next to strong spiritual truth.

questions.question: What rule does the passage give about judging a subject?
questions.answer: The judgment should come from people trained in that subject.

questions.question: What does the passage say about outsiders giving final judgments?
questions.answer: Their judgments should not be taken as decisive.

questions.question: How does the passage make this easy to understand?
questions.answer: It gives the example of an engineer and a doctor.

questions.question: Which one knows more about curing a disease?
questions.answer: The doctor.

questions.question: What kind of thinker is described as getting farther from spiritual truth?
questions.answer: A philosopher who is absorbed in only material things.

questions.question: What is his understanding limited by?
questions.answer: By only what he can physically observe.

questions.question: In spiritual and holy matters, who are presented as the reliable witnesses?
questions.answer: The People of Truth.

questions.question: What do these truthful people share with one another?
questions.answer: Agreement about the truths of faith.

questions.question: Why is Shaykh Gilani an important example in the passage?
questions.answer: He shows that some people reached very high spiritual certainty.

questions.question: What does the thunder-and-mosquito picture teach?
questions.answer: Strong truth overpowers weak denial.

questions.question: What main message should a 2nd grader remember from this passage?
questions.answer: People who truly know faith are better guides than people who only know worldly things.
